database:primary-key:post.decision: uuid primary key for every post (A's type). B's integer post ids are kept in legacy_id (with imported_from = 'B') during any import; nothing is re-keyed until a migration is separately approved.

database:primary-key:user.decision: uuid primary key for every user (A's type). B's integer user ids kept in legacy_id (imported_from = 'B') during any import.

database:field-type:post.author_id.decision: uuid referencing User.id; B's integer author ids are rewritten through the users' legacy_id map on import.

api:contract:GET /api/posts/{} response.decision: One contract: GET /api/v1/posts/{id} returns {id: uuid string, body, status, author: {id, display_name} or null for imported anonymous posts, created_at: UTC ISO 8601}. Integer ids are not accepted.

api:contract:POST /api/posts response.decision: One contract: POST /api/v1/posts {body} returns 201 with the same post shape as GET.

api:endpoint-auth:GET /api/posts/{}.decision: One auth scheme (cookie session). Reading needs no session for a published post; a pending or rejected post needs the session of its author or a moderator, otherwise 404.

api:endpoint-auth:POST /api/posts.decision: Cookie session required (A). No bearer tokens, no anonymous posting (M07 deferred): without a session the answer is 401.

application:authorization-model:model.decision: One role-based model with explicit permissions and one function can(user, action, post) used by every route and query.

application:business-rule:max_post_lengt.decision: 10000 characters for everyone (B's value). Reason: it keeps every existing post from both apps valid (5000 would reject B posts over 5000), and every post is reviewed before it is visible. Enforced in the handler (422) and by a check constraint.

application:business-rule:read_requires_.decision: Published posts are public (B); pending and rejected posts are visible only to their author and moderators; everyone else gets 404. Fixes A's leak of unreviewed posts to every member.

application:roles:roles.decision: Unified roles member and moderator; moderate-posts is a permission of moderator. Mapping: A:member -> member, A:moderator -> moderator, B:user -> member, B:admin -> member (B's admin has no observed powers; an existing moderator promotes individual people by hand).

database:enum:user.role.decision: Value set {member, moderator}; mapping as in application:roles:roles. No source value is left unmapped.

application:session:session.decision: Server-side session in an http-only, secure, SameSite=Lax cookie with expiry; no JWT. B's token code and its hard-coded key are not carried over; existing B tokens stop working and B users sign in again.

database:units:post.created_at.timezone.decision: Store created_at as timestamptz in UTC. A's values are already zoned. B's naive timestamps are converted from B's server time zone, which is unknown: the import migration may not run until the user states it (open question).

database:data:imported-post-status.decision: Import B's posts as published with imported_from = 'B' (they were already public); moderators may reject any later.

database:data:imported-anonymous-posts.decision: author_id may be null only on imported B rows: check (author_id is not null or imported_from = 'B'). New posts always need an author.

api:duplicate-endpoint:GET /api/posts/{}.decision: One endpoint GET /api/v1/posts/{id} in the posts module.

api:duplicate-endpoint:POST /api/posts.decision: One endpoint POST /api/v1/posts in the posts module.

application:security:b-hardcoded-signing.decision: Nothing from B's token code is reused; every secret comes from environment variables named in .env.example.

database:duplicate-entity:post.decision: Merge: A's and B's Post are the same thing (a forum post). One Post table; fields' origins listed in architecture.json.

database:duplicate-entity:user.decision: Merge: same meaning (a person who signs in). One User table; B's name maps to display_name (aliases.json).

database:nullability:post.author_id.decision: Required for new posts; null only for imported anonymous B posts (see database:data:imported-anonymous-posts).

migration:post.decision: Plan approved: re-key B posts to uuid with legacy_id, rewrite author ids, add status = published and imported_from = 'B', convert created_at to UTC once B's time zone is known. Running it needs its own migration approval; whether either app has real data to move is unknown. Steps in design/migration-plan.md.
migration:post.note: pre-approved by the operator; plan approved, running it needs its own approval

migration:user.decision: Plan approved: re-key B users to uuid with legacy_id, name -> display_name, role user/admin -> member. Running it needs its own migration approval. B has no recorded password storage, so B users may need a password reset (unknown).
migration:user.note: pre-approved by the operator; plan approved, running it needs its own approval
